title: Add dependency_firewall_activity_stats table + model
description:
## What Adds the `dependency_firewall_activity_stats` table and its `Security::DependencyFirewallActivityStat` model — the persistence layer for the **Dependency Firewall activity dashboard** (beta). One row per `(rule, project, hour, outcome)` bucket, holding a running `count`. Migration, model, factory, dictionary and a dev seed ship together (GitLab's `Migration/EnsureFactoryForTable` cop and dictionary class-derivation require the model present alongside the migration). - Work item: [601558](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/601558) (architecture decision record in the comments). - Post-beta scale (ClickHouse): [#603733](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/603733) — out of scope for beta. ## MR chain Shipped as three stacked MRs (this is **MR 1**): | | MR | Scope | | --- | --- | --- | | **MR 1** | !241785 (this MR) | **DB schema** — the `dependency_firewall_activity_stats` table + model | | **MR 2** | !242529 ([#601559](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/601559)) | **Writes** — records block/warn/allow activity from the enforcement path (the `increment!` caller) | | **MR 3** | !242511 ([#601560](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/601560)) | **Reads** — exposes the data via GraphQL for the dashboard | Original end-to-end POC: !241386. ## Beta context for reviewers This is a **flag-gated beta** (`dependency_firewall_phase1` + `dependency_firewall` licence) for a small design-partner cohort. We deliberately chose a Postgres hourly pre-aggregated counter over per-event rows and over ClickHouse for beta; ClickHouse is the planned post-beta path ([#603733](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/603733)), kept additive via a single write seam. Full rationale + alternatives in the [601558](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/601558) decision record. ## Schema `dependency_firewall_activity_stats` — `gitlab_main_org`, sharding key `project_id`: | column | notes | | --- | --- | | `dependency_firewall_policy_rule_id` | **nullable** FK → rules (NULL = `allowed` / no rule matched) | | `project_id` | FK → projects (sharding key, triggering project) | | `stat_time` | `timestamptz`, start of the UTC **hour** bucket | | `outcome` | smallint enum: `blocked` / `warned` / `allowed` | | `count` | running total for the bucket | - Unique index `(dependency_firewall_policy_rule_id, project_id, stat_time, outcome)` **NULLS NOT DISTINCT** — the `ON CONFLICT` upsert arbiter *and* the per-rule read index. - Index `(project_id, stat_time)` — group aggregation + project FK coverage. - 3 reversible migrations: create table, then one FK per migration via `add_concurrent_foreign_key` (`disable_ddl_transaction!`). Column ordering follows the 8-byte-first / smallint-last convention. `db/schema_migrations/` markers committed 1:1. ## Model surface - `belongs_to :dependency_firewall_policy_rule` (optional), `belongs_to :project`. - `enum :outcome` → `{ blocked: 0, warned: 1, allowed: 2 }`. - `.increment!(project_id:, outcome:, rule_id: nil, time:)` — one atomic `INSERT … ON CONFLICT … count + 1`, bucketed to the UTC hour. - Read aggregations `.outcome_totals`, `.activity_counts_by_rule`, `.activity_totals_by_rule` — each takes a `time_range:` (rolling window), returning bounded `SUM` queries. ## Recorded queries (`QUERY_RECORDER_DEBUG=1`) A dashboard load runs a **fixed 6 aggregate queries** (3 per-rule + 3 summary, one per outcome), independent of rule/row count. ```sql -- WRITE (increment! via upsert_all, one atomic upsert per event; rule_id NULL for allowed). -- stat_time is truncated to the UTC hour in Ruby; created_at/updated_at come from Rails timestamps. INSERT INTO dependency_firewall_activity_stats (dependency_firewall_policy_rule_id, project_id, stat_time, outcome, count, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, 1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) ON CONFLICT (dependency_firewall_policy_rule_id, project_id, stat_time, outcome) DO UPDATE SET count = dependency_firewall_activity_stats.count + 1, updated_at = now() RETURNING id; -- READ per-rule (activity_counts_by_rule, once per outcome) SELECT SUM(count) AS sum_count, dependency_firewall_policy_rule_id FROM dependency_firewall_activity_stats WHERE dependency_firewall_policy_rule_id IN ($rule_ids) AND project_id IN ($project_scope) AND stat_time BETWEEN $from AND $to AND outcome = $outcome GROUP BY dependency_firewall_policy_rule_id; -- READ summary (outcome_totals, once per outcome) SELECT SUM(count) FROM dependency_firewall_activity_stats WHERE project_id IN ($project_scope) AND stat_time BETWEEN $from AND $to AND outcome = $outcome; ``` `$project_scope` = `project_id = $id` (project) or the `projects → namespaces` traversal subquery (`Namespace#all_projects`) for a group. ## Query plans (`EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`) Gitlab DB Lab links: - https://console.postgres.ai/gitlab/projects/gitlab-production-main/sessions/53143/commands/155008 - https://console.postgres.ai/gitlab/projects/gitlab-production-main/sessions/53143/commands/155009 - https://console.postgres.ai/gitlab/projects/gitlab-production-main/sessions/53143/commands/155010 Captured against the table seeded with **21,603 hourly buckets** (~800 projects × hourly `stat_time` over 90 days × 3 outcomes × ~80 rules), in a rolled-back transaction with FK triggers bypassed. Params simulate a 50-project group over the last 24h. **Findings** - All three **reads** use `i_dep_fw_activity_stats_project_time (project_id, stat_time)` — the `Index Cond` includes the `stat_time` range, so the scan is **bounded by the rolling window, not table size** (~124–127 shared buffer hits, no seq scans, < 0.1 ms). - The **write** (`increment!`) uses `i_dep_fw_activity_stats_unique` as the **Conflict Arbiter Index** (`Tuples Inserted: 1`, 12 buffers).
READ — outcome_totals ``` Aggregate (cost=104.41..104.42 rows=1) (actual time=0.052..0.052 rows=1 loops=1) Buffers: shared hit=127 -> Nested Loop (actual time=0.021..0.045 rows=8 loops=1) -> HashAggregate (project_id IN list) rows=50 -> Index Scan using i_dep_fw_activity_stats_project_time (loops=50) Index Cond: ((project_id = ...) AND (stat_time >= now()-'24:00:00') AND (stat_time <= now())) Filter: (outcome = 2) ```
READ — activity_counts_by_rule / activity_totals_by_rule ``` GroupAggregate (actual time=0.056..0.058 rows=7 loops=1) Group Key: dependency_firewall_policy_rule_id Buffers: shared hit=124 -> Hash Semi Join (rule_id IN list) -> Nested Loop -> HashAggregate (project_id IN list) rows=50 -> Index Scan using i_dep_fw_activity_stats_project_time (loops=50) Index Cond: ((project_id = ...) AND (stat_time >= now()-'24:00:00') AND (stat_time <= now())) ```
WRITE — increment! upsert ``` Insert on dependency_firewall_activity_stats (actual time=0.075..0.075 loops=1) Conflict Resolution: UPDATE Conflict Arbiter Indexes: i_dep_fw_activity_stats_unique Tuples Inserted: 1 Conflicting Tuples: 0 Buffers: shared hit=12 ```
## Access patterns, growth & availability (for database review) **Anticipated growth (3 / 6 / 12 months)** — bounded by `active_projects × hours_active × outcomes`, *not* by event volume (one row per `(rule/project, hour, outcome)` bucket regardless of throughput): - Beta is flag-gated to a small design-partner cohort → realistically **thousands of rows over 3–6 months**. - An always-active project contributes ≤ `24 × 365 × 3 ≈ 26k` rows/year. At GA the upper envelope is ~tens-to-low-hundreds of millions/year, capped by planned `stat_time` **retention + range-partitioning** (and the ClickHouse migration, [#603733](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/603733)). **Reads & writes per hour** — **Writes**: one atomic upsert per block/warn/allow event; `allowed` is high-volume but **coalesces into one hot row per `(project, hour, allowed)`**; beta volume is low. **Reads**: a fixed **6 bounded aggregate `SUM` queries** per dashboard load (on-demand), window-bounded so they stay flat as the table grows. **Availability risk**: low. Reads are window-bounded; the only scale risk is hot-bucket write contention on high-volume `allowed`, mitigated by a planned Redis buffer + flush and ultimately ClickHouse ([#603733](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/work_items/603733)). The design scales for the beta cohort; GA scaling is the documented follow-up. ## Tests `ee/spec/models/security/dependency_firewall_activity_stat_spec.rb` — **19 examples, all passing** (associations, validations, enum, atomic upsert/hourly bucketing, NULL-rule `allowed` coalescing, and the three windowed read aggregations). `db/fixtures/development/40_dependency_firewall_activity_stats.rb` seeds the table for local dev + upgrade testing.
